name: Safety First!

pick.label: Pick a danger
pick.heading: Pick a danger and run a campaign
lead: Governments have spent decades warning us about things: smoking, speeding, sunburn, not washing our hands. Some of those campaigns are so famous that people still quote them.
Choose an everyday danger from the shelf, or find your own, and design a public safety campaign about it. Most of these dangers are very small. *Treat them as if they were enormous.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously I am not looking for a serious public health strategy here, this is just for a bit of fun. The more dramatically you warn people about something tiny, the better.

shelf.head: Berlin hazards
items: Stopping at the top of the escalator
Broken glass after New Year’s Eve

shelf.head: Student life
items: Forgetting your laundry in the machine

rows: Which danger from the shelf (or your own) are you warning people about?
Who keeps doing it? Be precise: where, when, and why they never learn.
Short enough to remember, and ideally a bit annoying, so it sticks.
A cartoon animal, a celebrity, a very serious man in a suit?
Posters, a TikTok, a jingle on the radio, stickers on the escalator, somewhere nobody expects?
What would you count, and who would do the counting?

values.danger: Stopping at the top of the escalator
values.who: Everyone at Alexanderplatz between 8 and 9am, especially people who have just realised they don’t know which exit they need.
values.mascot: Klaus, a very polite penguin who stops at the top of every escalator to check Google Maps and causes a ten-penguin pile-up every morning.
values.where: On the escalator steps themselves, so you read the slogan one step at a time. The last step says: KEEP WALKING, KLAUS.
values.worked: I’d stand at the top of the escalator at Alex with a clipboard and count the pile-ups. I would cause several of them myself.

yours.label: Your campaign
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your campaign in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which campaign wins?
rank.placeholder: The campaign, e.g. Don’t stop at the top
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their campaign in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
